**Observations**

- **Output biases (b3) show a fixed black frame.** The whole outer ring is strongly negative: row 0 is about -0.40 to -0.52, column 0 is -0.34 to -0.54 (for example pixels 12, 24, 36, 48), column 11 is around -0.45 to -0.53, and the bottom row is -0.10 to -0.46. The interior biases sit near 0, between about -0.10 and +0.07 (for example pixel 55: 0.018, 63: 0.049, 66: 0.048, 87: 0.069). So the border is always black, and interior pixels are white roughly half the time, which points to filled shapes rather than thin outlines.
- **Several W3 rows are clean slanted edges running down-left from the top middle:**
  - h2 unit 13: pixel 17 (r1,c5) 0.129; 28/29 (r2,c4/c5) 0.112/0.136; 40 (r3,c4) 0.328; 51 (r4,c3) 0.282; 63 (r5,c3) 0.368; 74 (r6,c2) 0.450; 86 (r7,c2) 0.457; 98 (r8,c2) 0.351.
  - h2 unit 46 has a negative band with positives to its right: 54/55 (r4,c6/c7) -0.206/-0.414; 66 (r5,c6) -0.497; 77/78 (r6,c5/c6) -0.289/-0.587; 89 (r7,c5) -0.614; 100/101 (r8,c4/c5) -0.321/-0.424; 112 (r9,c4) -0.396. The positives are 80 at 0.211, 91 to 93 at about 0.19 to 0.25, and 102 to 105 at about 0.14 to 0.20.
  - Units 3 and 49 have the same kind of negative diagonal, at r3 to r9, c5 to c2, with mild positives on the right.
- **Other rows are mirror-image edges running down-right:**
  - h2 unit 20: 18 (r1,c6) 0.350; 30/31 (r2,c6/c7) 0.250/0.299; 43 (r3,c7) 0.464; 56 (r4,c8) 0.387; 68 (r5,c8) 0.318; 81 (r6,c9) 0.419; 93/94 (r7,c9/c10) 0.23; 106 (r8,c10) 0.301.
  - h2 unit 33: 44 at 0.556, 56/57 at 0.461/0.396, 69 at 0.619, 81/82 at 0.341/0.393, with negatives on the inner left side (52 to 54 and 64, about -0.10 to -0.14).
- **Other rows are horizontal edges near the bottom:**
  - h2 unit 21: row 10 (pixels 121 to 130) is +0.17 to +0.40.
  - h2 unit 11: row 8 is positive (pixel 101 at 0.273) and row 9 (pixels 109 to 117) is -0.24 to -0.42.
  - h2 unit 40: row 7 (pixels 86 to 94) is +0.14 to +0.47.
  - h2 unit 37: row 9 positive, 0.455 at pixel 110.
- **Many h2 units add a uniform negative offset to every pixel** (units 4, 15, 26, 27, 44, 59, 63). This is a global "darken everything" component.

**Reasoning**

- The features are edges with a dark side and a bright side, not thin ridges. Together with interior biases near 0, this means filled white regions on black, not outlines.
- The only oblique edges are of two kinds, and they meet near the top middle:
  - one family goes down-left from about (r1, c5);
  - the mirror family goes down-right from about (r1, c6).
- The only other edges are horizontal ones near the bottom, at rows 7 to 10.
- That combination describes a filled triangle with its apex up and a horizontal base. It rules out circles (no curved edges), rectangles (no vertical edges), and inverted triangles (the slants converge at the top).
- The slopes are about 3 to 4 columns per 7 rows on each side, roughly symmetric. So the triangle is a fairly tall isosceles one.
- The edge families appear at several offsets (for example, apex rows 1 to 3 and base rows 7 to 10). So size and position vary somewhat, but the triangle always stays inside the always-black one-pixel border.

**Images**

- Each image is a single solid white, upright, roughly isosceles triangle on a black background.
- The apex is near the top center, around row 1 to 3 and column 5 or 6.
- The base is horizontal, near the bottom, around row 8 to 10, and spans roughly columns 2 to 10.
- It is typically about 7 to 9 rows tall and 7 to 9 pixels wide at the base.
- The outer border pixels are always black.

**Example**
